thread:
sophia.li: Heads up — got a spike in CI fails for the eval harness after the infra deploy at 09:12UTC. Failing model: redwood-13B-int8-v2, metric: semantic-sim (cosine). Fail rate went from 0.7% -> 9.8% for the nightly suite.
sophia.li: I ran a local smoke with the same model and seed; reproduces. Outputs look shifted — embeddings are systematically lower magnitude and some near-zero vectors where they used to be ~0.8 norm.
akshay.patel: any error logs? or is it purely numerical drift?
sophia.li: purely numerical drift. no exceptions. snippet from harness:```
AssertionError: mean_cosine >= 0.5 (0.423)
Expected ~0.71
Test case: semantic-sim/subset-A/seed-42
Model binary hash: runner@sha256:7f2a1d...
Tokenizer ref: tokenizers@ref:2026-03-18-8f3b
```
jonathan.kim: CI deploy at 09:12 shows two changelists: infra/runner: pick up kernel-fix (r=U205) and tool/tokenizers: bump ref to 2026-03-18. Which one landed first?
ci-bot: deploy: prod-infra at 09:12 UTC — commits: runner@7f2a1d, tokenizers@8f3b2c. No other changes.
maria.ops: If it's tokenizer-related, impact is broad. Hold any model rollouts until investigated. :warning:
akshay.patel: quick check — if embeddings magnitude changed, tokenization differences (BPE offsets, special token handling) are a likely suspect. Can you paste the token counts for the failing examples?
sophia.li: here: `input_len -> tokens` for two failing cases: "How do I reset my DNS?" -> 11 used to be 12; "translate to fr: Hello" -> 4 used to be 5. So some whitespace handling or language prefix tokenization changed.
jonathan.kim: that lines up with tokenizers@2026-03-18 doing a trimming normalization patch. Might remove leading spaces around colons. But why would that change embedding magnitude so much? Could be that the position of EOS or special tokens shifted upstream and pooling picks different subtoken to represent sentence.
akshay.patel: we should bisect between the two commits in CI to isolate. Steps: 1) run harness with runner@previous + tokenizers@new; 2) run with runner@new + tokenizers@previous. That will tell which component causes it. I can spin up the two tries.
sophia.li: starting job now: `./scripts/eval_run --model redwood-13B-int8-v2 --tokenizer tokenizers@8f3b2c --runner runner@7f2a1d --suite semantic-sim/subset-A`
(eval-bot): job 98763 queued on ci-small - started 09:25 UTC
(eval-bot): job 98763 done: fail rate 9.6% (same)
jonathan.kim: try the other combo please.
sophia.li: running `--tokenizer tokenizers@prev --runner runner@7f2a1d` (runner old, tokenizer old) -> baseline passes.
sophia.li: running `--tokenizer tokenizers@prev --runner runner@7f2a1d` actually that was baseline. Now `--tokenizer tokenizers@prev --runner runner@new` (runner new, tokenizer old) -> pass still.
sophia.li: conclusion: tokenizers@8f3b2c causes the drift.
akshay.patel: thanks — so tokenization change is culprit. For short term: pin tokenizer ref in CI for eval harness to previous stable ref and re-run nightly. Long term: need to add tokenization-sensitive regression tests (round-trip token counts + embedding-norm checks) before tokenizers bumps.
maria.ops: create a blocker ticket for release-ops to pin and block rollouts until we patch the tokenizer.
oncall: @maria.ops filed INFRA-4021 blocking rollouts and notifying PMs.
johnathan.kim: can we craft a focused unit test? Something like minimal seed inputs that exercise leading/trailing-space behavior and assert stable token counts and embedding norm (within epsilon). If tokenizers team intends the normalization, we need to update retrain/eval expectations and document change.
akshay.patel: I'll draft a test: `tests/tokenizer_regressions/test_normalization_sanity.py` with a table of inputs and expected token sequences and embedding-norm thresholds.
sophia.li: created reproducer and opened PR #5147 to pin tokenizer ref in eval CI: https://git.redwood.dev/redwood/inference-ci/pull/5147 — please review.
akshay.patel: quick mitigation approved: roll back tokenizer ref in the eval CI config, re-run nightly, and hold broad model rollouts until we decide.
maria.ops: noted, scheduling canary reruns at 10:30 UTC once pin lands.
jonathan.kim: follow-ups: (1) coordinate with tokenizers owners — understand if change was intentional, (2) add gating in our CI for tokenizer ref bumps (automated diff of token counts + sample embed sanity), (3) update changelog for model bring-up docs explaining tokenizer ref coupling.
sophia.li: thanks all — for now we have a clear root cause and a mitigation PR. Will post updates after canary. :white_check_mark:
